findings.file: tests/_harness.py:805-826 (run's print(text)), reached from replay_selftest at 1232-1262
findings.issue: The replay now escapes what each block PRINTED (res out/err) through encodable, but the replay's own report is still written strictly: run() does print(text) of a _render() whose FAIL lines carry each failing case's label and detail, and those details are text the child produced and the sweep decoded as UTF-8 (a %r or str of a value holding an arrow or U+FFFD). Under the same strict cp1252 stdout a failing replayed case with such a detail still raises out of print(text), hiding the tally behind the same 0/1 the change set out to remove. It only bites when a case is already failing, so a green run is unaffected; sr19 covers the out path only, not a failing detail.
findings.resolution: Write the rendered text through encodable(text, sys.stdout) in run() (or reconfigure the stream with errors=backslashreplace once at the replay's entry), and add a case beside sr19 whose replayed block FAILS with a non-cp1252 detail and still prints the exact tally under PYTHONIOENCODING=cp1252.

intent.note: Task clauses: (a) 'writes replayed output through encodable, which escapes what the stream cannot spell, so the tally stays exact' - tests/_harness.py encodable() encodes with backslashreplace in the stream's own codec and replay_results wraps both stdout and stderr writes (lines 1114-1143); sr19 shows exit 0 with x1,x2,y1 and ALL PASS 3/3 under PYTHONIOENCODING=cp1252, sr19b shows cp1252 keeps e-acute and escapes the other two while UTF-8 keeps all. (b) 'keeps a timed-out block's partial output for the replay (run_one's partial)' - run_one sets partial = child_text(exc.stdout or b'') on TimeoutExpired, block_entry passes it as out only when code is None (tools/sweep-selftests.py:1195-1228, 1718-1727); tt3c asserts the partial line appears exactly once. (c) 'refuses by name any job whose start falls after the sweep's deadline, giving a replay at least REPLAY_RESERVE' - child() returns not_started when remaining <= 0 and not reserve, and a replay gets max(1, reserve, ceil(remaining)); a suite none of whose blocks started becomes one not_started row with no replay (1834-1871); tt3b checks the refused row's why/output and seconds None. (d) 'rounded up, not truncated' - int(-(-remaining // 1)); this is also what makes tt3b deterministic, since a 3s-cut job now ends past the deadline. I traced a refused row through claude_verdicts (skipped: no windows/began_ns), costs_from_rows (skipped: seconds None, line 1627), suite_ran (sums only ran blocks), and the render's seconds guard (line 2021): all accept it.
